Coffee grinder care

A clean grinder makes better coffee. Here's the short version.

How often should I clean it?
Every week if you grind daily. Every few days if you use oily dark roasts.
What do I need?
Dry rice or grinder tablets, a stiff brush, and a damp cloth. No water inside the burr chamber.
Step by step
  1. Unplug it.
  2. Empty the hopper and grounds bin.
  3. Run a small handful of dry rice or a tablet through.
  4. Brush out the chute and burrs.
  5. Wipe the exterior with a damp cloth.
Can I wash the parts?
Only the hopper and bin if the manual says they're removable and washable. Burrs stay dry.
How do I know it's clean?
No stale smell, no visible grounds, and the next dose tastes like the beans, not yesterday's.

If it's been years, consider replacing the burrs. They dull.

Most clogs live in the P-trap. You can usually fix it without calling anyone.

Boil a kettle and pour it slowly down the drain. Wait five minutes. Repeat. This melts grease.
Then try baking soda and vinegar
Pour half a cup of baking soda, then half a cup of white vinegar. Let it fizz for 15 minutes. Flush with hot water.

Put a bucket under the trap. Unscrew the slip nuts by hand. Clean out the gunk. Reassemble hand-tight.

If multiple drains are slow, or you see water backing up elsewhere, the clog is deeper in the line.

Skip chemical drain cleaners if you have older pipes. They're harsh.

Keep herbs fresh

Two methods: soft herbs and hard herbs.

Soft herbs (basil, cilantro, parsley)
Treat them like flowers. Trim the stems, put them in a glass of water, cover loosely with a plastic bag, and refrigerate. Change the water every couple of days.
Hard herbs (rosemary, thyme, oregano)
Wrap them in a slightly damp paper towel, then in a plastic bag. Store in the crisper drawer.
Basil is special
Basil hates cold. Leave it on the counter in water, like a bouquet.
Freeze extra

Unclog a Vacuum Filter

Loss of suction is usually a clogged filter, not a dying motor. Here's the fix, user_name.

Quick check: if suction returns when the filter is out (don't run it long that way), the filter is your culprit.
How do I know the filter is the problem?
Weak pick-up, a hot exhaust, a musty smell, or visible dust on the pleats. Machines that used to grab a rug now just skim it.
Can I wash a HEPA filter?
Only if it says washable. Rinse from the clean side with cool water until it runs clear. Never use soap or a brush, and never put it in the dryer or a hot oven. Air-dry 24 hours, bone dry, before it goes back in. Damp pleats breed mildew.
Dry-only filters?
Tap them gently over a bin and brush the pleats with a soft dry brush. Replace every 3-6 months, sooner if you have pets or fine dust.

Drying timeline

  • 0 hRinse, shake off excess.
  • 4 hTurn it over once.
  • 24 hFully dry, tap and reinstall.
A wet filter in a running vacuum can fry the motor. When in doubt, wait another night.

After every third wash, check the replacement date on the housing.

Fix a Squeaky Door Hinge

That squeak is metal on metal, dry and complaining. Lube, and it quiets down, user_name.

What should I use?
A drop of light machine oil, silicone spray, or lithium grease. Cooking oil works in a pinch but goes gummy and attracts dust. WD-40 helps briefly; it cleans more than it lubricates.
How do I apply it?
Wipe the hinge clean first. Open the door to take pressure off, then place one drop at the top of each hinge pin and one at the bottom. Swing the door back and forth a dozen times so it works in. Wipe the drip.
Still squeaking?
Pull the pin with a punch or a nail and a hammer, wipe it, grease it, and tap it back. If the hinge is loose, tighten the screws, or swap in longer ones. A stripped screw hole gets a wooden matchstick and glue as a plug.
Only touch hinges on a door you can support. A heavy door off its pin is a bad afternoon.
  1. Clean the hinge.
  2. One drop per pin, top and bottom.
  3. Swing the door to spread it.
  4. Wipe the excess.

Repeat once a year, more in humid rooms.

Stale is not spoiled. Starch just re-crystallised, and heat can undo it, user_name.

Rule of thumb: dry heat for crusty loaves, moisture for soft ones.
Crusty loaf or baguette
Run it under the tap for two seconds, or flick water over the crust. Bake at 180°C / 350°F for 8-10 minutes. The crust crackles back, the inside softens. Eat it the same day; it stales again faster the second time.
Soft sandwich bread
Skip the oven. Wrap a slice in a damp paper towel and microwave 10-15 seconds. Or steam it over a pot for a minute. It'll be tender, not toasted.
What if it's beyond saving?
Hard as a brick and dry through? Make croutons, breadcrumbs, or a panzanella. Toss cubes with oil, salt, and herbs, bake at 180°C for 12 minutes. Nothing wasted.

Stop Glasses From Fogging

Fog is warm breath hitting cool glass. Break that meeting and the lenses stay clear, user_name.

With a face mask
Pinch the nose wire snug against your cheeks, and pull the top edge high, under your glasses. Tuck the bottom under your chin. Tape the top edge if it's a loose cloth mask. The goal is no breath escaping upward.
Everyday anti-fog
A drop of dish soap rubbed on both sides, then buffed dry, leaves an invisible film that stops droplets forming. Shaving foam works the same way. Commercial anti-fog sprays last longer but cost more.
Cooking and hot drinks
Warm the lenses first. A few seconds over steam or in a pocket raises their temperature so breath can't condense. Tilt your head back over the pot instead of leaning in.
Why do coatings matter?
Anti-reflective coatings fog more easily than bare lenses because the surface is rougher at a microscopic level. Clean with a microfibre cloth, not a shirt tail, which adds oils that trap moisture.
Best combo: snug mask plus a soap film. Two defences beat one.

Reapply the soap film every couple of days.

Where do I start?

Two free opt-outs cover most of it:

  2. DMAchoice — dmachoice.org, small fee, handles catalogs and coupon packs.

Call the 800 number printed on the catalog's back cover and ask for "permanent removal." It's faster than any registry, and they honor it. One call per brand.

Unclog a Vacuum

Loss of suction is almost always one of four things.

Check the filter first

Pull it out and look through it against a light. If light won't pass, neither will air. Rinse foam filters in cool water and dry 24 hours — a damp filter smells like a wet dog and can damage the motor.

Then the hose and wand

Drop a coin or a small screw down the hose and listen for it landing. No sound? Something's stuck. A broom handle or a straightened coat hanger clears most blockages. Check the elbow bend, where clogs love to hide.

The brush roll

Flip the vacuum and cut hair off the roller with scissors. Long hair wrapped tight is the #1 cause of a burning smell. Never pull it with your hands.

Burning smell — is it dead?
Stop using it. A burnt smell usually means a stretched belt or a hot motor. Replace the belt (cheap), and if the smell returns, retire the vacuum.
How often should I do all this?

Filters monthly, brush roll every few weeks, hose only when suction drops. user_name, a two-minute habit beats a new vacuum every year.

Can I use soap?

Yes, a little. Modern dish soap won't strip seasoning. What wrecks it is soaking, scraping with metal, or leaving it wet.

Everyday cleaning

  2. Dry on the stove over low heat for 2 minutes.

It's rusty. Now what?

Scour the rust off with steel wool or salt and oil, wash, dry, then re-season. Rust is a surface problem, not a funeral.

How do I season it?

Rub a very thin layer of flaxseed or canola oil all over, inside and out, then bake upside down at 450°F for an hour. Repeat 3–4 times. Thin coats, hot oven, patience.

Sticky spots?

That's too much oil baked on. Scrub it back to bare metal in that spot and season again. user_name, less oil than you think.

Door sticks near the top or bottom

Tighten every hinge screw first. If one spins loose, fill the hole with a wooden matchstick or toothpick dipped in glue, snap it off, and re-drive the screw.

It rubs along the whole frame

The house has shifted or the door swelled. Lightly sand the sticking edge, seal it with primer, and check again in a week. Seasonal swelling often fixes itself.

Revive Dead Batteries

You can't bring a battery back to life. You can make the next one last.

What's actually killing it?

Heat, mostly. A phone left on a hot dashboard ages faster in one afternoon than a month of normal use. Screen brightness and background location are the other two big draws.

Charging habits that help
  • Stay between 20% and 80% when you can.
  • Skip the overnight trickle if your phone charges fast.
  • Take the case off while fast-charging — heat has nowhere to go.
Does a new charger matter?

Use the one that came with your device or a certified equivalent. Cheap unbranded bricks can overheat the battery quietly.

Is my battery already worn out?

Check the battery health in settings. Under 80% of original capacity means it's near the end. Replacement is usually cheap and often worth it over a new device.

One weird trick?

Lower the screen brightness to about 50% and turn off always-on display. user_name, that alone buys most people an extra hour.

Old grounds go stale and make fresh coffee taste off. A quick clean keeps every cup tasting like the first.

  1. Unplug the grinder.

Why is my computer slow?

Usually it's too many startup programs, a nearly full drive, or background updates. Rarely is it the hardware itself.

What should I do first?

Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) and check the Startup tab. Disable anything you don't need at login. That alone can cut boot time in half.

How do I free up space?

Run Disk Cleanup (or Storage Sense on Windows 10/11) and clear temporary files. Aim to keep at least 15% of your drive empty.

Are browser tabs the problem?

Yes, often. Each tab eats memory. Try an extension like OneTab or just close what you're not reading.

Only if you have a spinning hard drive. If you have an SSD, don't defrag—it's unnecessary and adds wear. Windows optimizes SSDs automatically.

Run a full scan with Windows Defender or Malwarebytes. Adware and crypto miners are common causes of sudden slowness.

Should I reinstall Windows?

It's a last resort. Try the steps above first. A clean install takes an afternoon and you'll lose apps, so back up first.

When is it time for new hardware?

If you have an old spinning drive, swapping to an SSD is the single biggest upgrade. If you're already on SSD and still slow, more RAM might help.

Wash cold, by hand or on a wool cycle. Never tumble dry. Dry flat, always.

Season a New Nonstick Pan

Nonstick pans don't need polymerised seasoning like cast iron, but a quick warm-up wipe removes factory residue and helps the coating last.

Why it matters

New pans carry a thin manufacturing film. That's the smell and the grey rag you get on the first wash. It isn't dangerous, just unappetising.

The five-minute routine
  1. Wash with warm water and a soft sponge. No steel wool, ever.
  2. Dry it, then set it on medium heat for two minutes.
  3. Add a teaspoon of neutral oil and swirl to coat.
  4. Wipe with a paper towel and let it cool.
  5. Wipe once more to remove excess oil.
Everyday rules
  • Medium heat is the ceiling. High heat kills coatings.
  • No metal utensils, no dishwasher.
  • Let it cool before washing, and never plunge a hot pan in cold water.

user_name, a well-kept nonstick pan lasts years. A mistreated one lasts a month and change.

When to replace it

If food sticks in the middle no matter what, or the coating is flaking, retire it. Flakes are not a great condiment.

Find the entry point

Watch a single ant for 30 seconds. It will walk back to the gap it came through — usually a skirting board joint, window frame, or along a pipe.

Seal the way in

Silicone along skirting gaps and pipe entries. Ants can squeeze through one millimetre.

Keep them gone

Wipe counters, tip the bin often, and store sugar in sealed jars. Boring, but it's the whole trick.

Step 1 — lift the wax

Scrape off any excess with a blunt knife or a credit card. Then press a paper towel onto the mark and hold a warm iron over it. The wax transfers to the towel. Repeat with a clean patch of towel each time.

  2. Work from the outside of the stain inward, so you don't spread the edge.
  3. Rinse with cool water and check before drying.
For stubborn marks

Go over it with a little isopropyl alcohol on a cotton pad. Test on an inside seam first, user_name — some dyes dislike the stuff.

No dryer and no hot air until the mark is fully gone. Heat sets wax stains permanently.

For upholstery

Same order of work, but blot instead of soak. Keep fabric barely damp and dry it with a towel rather than a hairdryer.

  • Don't pour cold water into a hot pot — it can warp or crack.
  • No metal scrapers on nonstick.

Stop a Toilet From Running

A running toilet is just water sneaking past a worn flapper. You can fix it in 15 minutes.

Why does my toilet keep running?

Most likely the flapper (the rubber seal at the bottom of the tank) isn't sealing. Water trickles into the bowl, the fill valve kicks on to top up the tank, and the cycle repeats. Other culprits: a stuck fill valve, a float set too high, or a warped flush valve seat.

How do I diagnose the problem?
  1. Lift the tank lid. Flush and watch.
  2. If water continues to flow into the bowl after the flush, the flapper is leaking.
  3. If the water level rises above the overflow tube, the fill valve or float needs adjusting.
What's the quick fix for a flapper?

Turn off the water supply, flush to empty the tank, then unhook the old flapper and take it to the hardware store to match. Install the new one, turn water back on, and test. If the flapper looks fine, try cleaning it and the valve seat with a cloth and some white vinegar.

How do I adjust the fill valve?

If the water level is too high, pinch the clip on the float rod and slide the float down a bit. For newer valves, turn the adjustment screw. The water should stop about an inch below the top of the overflow tube.

When should I call a plumber?

If you've replaced the flapper and adjusted the valve but it still runs, the flush valve seat may be damaged. That's a bigger job. Also call if you see water pooling around the base—that's a wax ring issue.

Water saved: up to 200 gallons a day. Your water bill will thank you, user_name.

Season a New Nonstick Pan

Nonstick pans don't need seasoning like cast iron, but a little prep helps them last.

Does a nonstick pan need seasoning?

Not in the traditional sense. The nonstick coating is already slick. But washing off manufacturing residue and applying a thin layer of oil can improve performance and longevity.

How to prep a new nonstick pan
  1. Wash with warm soapy water and a soft sponge. Rinse and dry.
  2. Put the pan on low heat for 30 seconds to ensure it's dry.
  3. Add a teaspoon of neutral oil (like canola) and wipe it around with a paper towel.
  4. Heat on low for another minute, then wipe off excess oil.
  5. Let it cool, then it's ready to use.
Can I use butter or olive oil?

For seasoning, use a high-smoke-point oil like canola, grapeseed, or vegetable oil. Butter and extra-virgin olive oil burn at lower temperatures and leave a sticky residue.

How often should I re-season?

Only if the pan starts sticking. A quick wipe with oil after each wash (while warm) can help maintain the surface. Avoid high heat and metal utensils to keep the coating intact.

What not to do
  • Don't use cooking spray—it leaves a gummy buildup.
  • Don't preheat an empty pan on high heat.
  • Don't put it in the dishwasher.
  • Don't stack other pans on top without protection.

Treat it gently and it'll treat you to years of easy eggs, user_name.

Ants in the kitchen are a pain. Here's how to send them packing without harsh chemicals.

Why are ants in my kitchen?

They're looking for food, water, or shelter. Even a tiny crumb or a leaky pipe can invite them in. They leave pheromone trails, so if you see one, more are on the way.

How do I find where they're coming from?

Follow the trail. They usually enter through cracks, windows, or gaps around pipes. Look for a line of ants moving to and from a source. Once you find the entry point, you can block it.

What's the best bait?

Use a slow-acting bait so they carry it back to the nest. Mix 1 part borax with 3 parts sugar, add a little water to make a paste. Put it on small pieces of cardboard near the trail. They'll take it home and share. Keep pets and kids away.

How to keep them from coming back
  • Wipe counters and sweep floors after meals.
  • Store food in sealed containers.
  • Fix leaky faucets.
  • Seal cracks with caulk.
  • Rinse recycling before tossing.
Do natural repellents work?

Vinegar, lemon juice, or cinnamon can disrupt their trails, but they're temporary. For a real fix, you need to eliminate the colony. Bait is your best bet.

Stay persistent, user_name. A few days of baiting should do it.

Lipstick stains are waxy and pigmented. Here's how to lift them without spreading.

What should I do first?

Don't rub. Blot gently with a clean cloth to remove excess. Then treat with a grease-fighting dish soap and a stain remover.

Step-by-step removal
  1. Scrape off any solid lipstick with a dull knife.
  2. Apply a few drops of liquid dish soap directly onto the stain.
  3. Work it in gently with your fingers or a soft brush.
  4. Let it sit for 10 minutes.
  5. Rinse with warm water (not hot, which can set the stain).
  6. If any color remains, apply a pretreat stain remover or a paste of baking soda and water.
  7. Wash as usual, but check before drying—heat sets stains.
What about delicate fabrics?

For silk or wool, use a gentle method: dab with a cloth dipped in rubbing alcohol or vodka. Test first in a hidden spot. Then hand wash with a mild detergent.

Can I use hairspray?

Hairspray can work on some fabrics because of its alcohol content, but it can also leave a sticky residue. Rubbing alcohol is a better choice.

What if the stain is old?

Old lipstick stains may need multiple treatments. Try applying a commercial stain remover and let it sit for 15 minutes before washing. Repeat if necessary. Don't iron until the stain is gone.

Clean Burned-On Rice From a Pot

Burnt rice happens. Don't scrub—loosen it with a gentle simmer.

Why does rice burn?

Too little water, too high heat, or not enough stirring. The starch at the bottom caramelizes and sticks. It's a pain, but the pot is usually salvageable.

How to remove burned rice
  1. Fill the pot with water, covering the burnt layer by an inch.
  2. Add a few tablespoons of baking soda and a squirt of dish soap.
  3. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer for 10-15 minutes.
  4. Turn off heat and let it sit for an hour.
  5. Most of the burnt rice should lift off with a wooden spoon.
  6. If not, repeat or use a plastic scraper.
What if it's really stubborn?

Try a vinegar soak: fill with equal parts water and white vinegar, bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes. The acid helps break down the burnt bits. For stainless steel, you can use a non-scratch scrub pad.

Can I use oven cleaner?

Only on stainless steel or enamel, and with good ventilation. Spray, let sit, then rinse thoroughly. Never use on aluminum—it will pit the surface.

How to prevent burning next time
  • Use a heavy-bottomed pot.
  • Rinse rice until water runs clear.
  • Use the right water-to-rice ratio (usually 2:1).
  • Bring to a boil, then reduce to low and cover.
  • Don't stir too much—it makes rice gummy.

No need to toss the pot, user_name. A little patience and it'll be good as new.

Remove Hard Water Stains From Glass

Hard water stains are mineral deposits. Acid is your friend here.

What are hard water stains?

They're calcium and magnesium deposits left behind when water evaporates. They etch into glass over time, so the sooner you tackle them, the easier they come off.

How to remove them with vinegar
  1. Mix equal parts white vinegar and water in a spray bottle.
  2. Spray generously on the glass.
  3. Let it sit for 10-15 minutes.
  4. Wipe with a microfiber cloth.
  5. For stubborn spots, make a paste of vinegar and baking soda, apply, and scrub gently.
What about commercial removers?

Products with citric acid or sulfamic acid work well. Look for "hard water stain remover" or "lime scale remover." Always test on a small area and follow instructions.

Can I use a razor blade?

Yes, on glass only. Use a new razor blade at a 45-degree angle with soapy water as lubricant. It's great for tough spots, but don't use on tempered glass (like car windows) as it can scratch.

How to prevent future stains
  • Squeegee after every shower.
  • Dry glass immediately after cleaning.
  • Consider a water softener or a rinse aid.
  • Apply a rain-repellent coating to shower glass.

Sparkling glass is just a vinegar spray away, user_name.
